An educational model based on Chinese Pharmacopoeia dose ranges, German Commission E / EMA monographs and TCM materia medica theory. It does not replace diagnosis by a qualified practitioner. With a chronic condition, current medication, pregnancy, or for children, consult a physician or pharmacist first.

Nature is scored Cold −2, Cool −1.2, Slightly cold −1, Neutral 0, Slightly warm +1, Warm +1.5, Hot +2, Very hot +3. Extraction rate is the share of active constituents transferred to the liquid in one pass; solid–liquid equilibrium caps it at about 30–55% for a proper first decoction and 50–70% after a second boil. Potency = grams ÷ usual-dose midpoint × (this extraction ÷ standard-preparation extraction). Five-Phase shares combine the five flavors (sour→Wood, bitter→Fire, sweet→Earth, pungent→Metal, salty→Water) and the meridian organs, half each.

A Li Dongyuan formula. A large dose of Huangqi strongly tonifies spleen and lung qi to support the source of blood production ("tangible blood is born from intangible qi"), paired with Danggui to nourish blood and harmonize the nutritive level. Original ratio Huangqi : Danggui = 5:1 (30g : 6g).

From Yixue Qiyuan: ginseng tonifies qi, Maidong nourishes yin and clears heat, Wuweizi preserves yin and stops sweating; one tonifies, one moistens, one astringes, together augmenting qi and generating fluids. Using American Ginseng gives a gentler, cooler tonic suited to summer damage of both qi and yin.

The foundational qi tonic from Taiping Huimin Hejiju Fang. Ginseng is the chief, tonifying original qi; Baizhu is the deputy, strengthening the spleen and drying dampness; Fuling is the assistant, draining dampness; Gancao is the envoy, harmonizing the middle.

The foundational blood-tonifying and blood-regulating formula. Shudi and Baishao are "blood herbs within the blood"; Danggui and Chuanxiong are "qi herbs within the blood", so it tonifies without causing stagnation.
Jade Windscreen Powder (Yu Ping Feng San), missing Fangfeng

Huangqi augments qi and consolidates the exterior, Baizhu strengthens the spleen; these form the core of Yu Ping Feng San. The original formula also includes Fangfeng (Saposhnikovia) to disperse wind.
Goji nourishes the kidney and liver (water), Chrysanthemum clears the liver and brightens the eyes (wood), embodying "nourishing water to moisten wood"; this is the core pair of Qi Ju Di Huang Wan.
The chief herbs of Sang Ju Yin: disperse wind-heat, clear the lung and brighten the eyes; commonly used for early-stage wind-heat cough.
Combines clearing heat and resolving toxicity with dispersing wind and brightening the eyes; suited to wind-heat with internal heat, sore throat and red eyes.

Fresh Ginger (acrid, warm) moves the defensive level; Jujube (sweet, warm) tonifies the nutritive level. Together they harmonize the nutritive and defensive qi, harmonize the stomach and stop vomiting; commonly used in Gui Zhi Tang and other formulas.
From Shang Han Lun: diffuses the lung and soothes the throat, expels phlegm and pus; commonly used for sore throat.
